newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper ends down sharply on LME losses.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper ends down sharply on LME losses.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended down sharply in active trading on Wednesday due to panic selling triggered by heavy overnight losses on the London Metal Exchange, traders said.
The most active February 1996 contract ended at an intra-day high of 18,990 yuan ($2,287) per tonne, down 590 yuan. It opened limit-down at 18,890.
November fell 360 to 18,720, December 400 to 18,800, January 550 to 18,950, March 560 to 19,040, April and May 520 to 19,080.
Combined volume rose sharply to 117,570 tonnes from 66,260.
Copper opened mostly limit-down and stayed at low levels for most of the session.
Traders said heavy LME losses triggered panic selling and copper was likely to begin a new downward movement.
"Panic stop-loss selling was responsible for today's sharp falls," one trader said. "The fact they were accompanied by heavy volume indicates further falls are possible."
"Rebounds over the past few days seem to have finished," a second trader said.
Traders said heavy losses were reasonable because of poor domestic long-term fundamentals, although stockpiles on the LME have dropped successively.
"Long position holders took advantage of falls in LME stockpiles to push copper up but this cannot change the poor fundamentals," a third trader said.
Analysts said copper is likely to test the 18,500-yuan level if it cannot find support at 19,000 yuan in the next few days.
Aluminium ended down. The only traded November contract fell 20 to 13,400 yuan with volume of 160 tonnes.
